theUnavailablePortDesign.parentDecision: An unready capability port on a match that may have started must NOT silently answer 'not started'; (c) capability-unavailable (port absent/unready) → typed refusal mapped to the existing blocked/quarantine state rather than legacy fallback.
theUnavailablePortDesign.whatWasImplemented: The parent's rule, with ONE consistent adjustment: `port absent` and `port unready` are SPLIT rather than lumped.

split.portAbsent: `not-started`. A store with no branch port (e.g. `InMemoryMatchStore`, which has none — `grep readEffectiveHead src/lib/multiplayer/server/InMemoryMatchStore.ts` returns zero hits) has no journal at all, so it cannot have mirrored anything. This is a statement, not a dodge. Lumping it into the refusal would have blocked recovery for EVERY match on that store kind, including plain legacy matches that never touched journal authority.
split.portUnreadyButPresent: `unavailable` → `blocked/'recovery-fact-read-failed'`. The store CAN journal, may already have started this match, and cannot say.

theUnavailablePortDesign.measuredConsequenceOfTheRefusal: THIS IS THE BLOCKER. `isCapabilityDbAvailable()` is `customCapabilityDb !== undefined || getSQLiteService().isInitialized()` (`durableCapabilityPorts.ts:59-60`). Production builds the store as `new DurableMatchStore()` with NO `capabilityDb` (`getDefaultMatchStore.ts:73`), so in any process that never initialized the campaign SQLiteService the probe is FALSE for every match — the shipped shape at mode `off`. The refusal therefore blocks recovery for ordinary legacy matches, not just possibly-started ones. Measured cost: 3 of the 11 regressions (`durableViewerDelivery PROCESS RESTART`, `hardenedTransport replay-window-after-recovery`, `rollback proof baseline-only`), all on matches that never used journal authority.
theUnavailablePortDesign.narrowingAttemptedAndDISPROVEN: A gate gating the refusal on `getLastCommandReceipt(matchId) != null` (rationale: only a committed batch can mirror, so a receipt-free match provably has no head) was implemented and measured. It does NOT work — `DBG-RECEIPT m-durable-restart-client true` for a legacy-path match in `durableViewerDelivery`, so a receipt is not evidence of the batch/mirror path. The narrowing was removed; no match-DB-local fact was found that separates 'could have mirrored' from 'never journalled'.
openOptions: (i) Owner revises the decision: `unavailable` answers `not-started` (S3a's silent false) at the recovery site too. Closes 3 of 11 regressions; leaves row 1 of the proof suite unachievable and the hole the parent named open.

(ii) Record 'this stream was mirrored' on the MATCH database at mirror time so the recovery site can distinguish the two cases without the capability db. That is new S1 surface, not a sub-prefix-(2) change.

(iii) Guarantee the capability database is open wherever recovery runs, and pin it. The S3a reviewer flagged option (c) as 'only acceptable with a real pin'; it is now DISPROVEN as a standing property — four existing suites recover with no capability db at all.

theSecondBlocker.name: sub-prefixes (2) and (3) are not separable at the recovery site
theSecondBlocker.measurement: With the unavailable-refusal REMOVED (repoint only), the four affected suites still fail 8 of 39: `journalAuthorityRecovery` ×4 and `journalAuthorityRollbackProof` ×4.
theSecondBlocker.why: Those suites drive real journal-authority commits on `InMemoryMatchStore` and on `new DurableMatchStore({ path })` with no capability database. No head is ever mirrored there, so the `mp_journal_authority_started` marker is their ONLY started record. Retiring the marker's authority at recovery — which is exactly what proof-suite row 4 pins and what the parent required ('decision follows the head, not the marker') — demotes those matches to `legacy-compatible` and their `isJournalAuthorityEnabled() === true` assertions fail.
theSecondBlocker.consequence: Proof-suite row 4 and those 8 assertions are the same coin. There is no implementation that satisfies both. Landing sub-prefix (2) requires migrating those 8 assertions onto capability-backed, actually-mirrored stores — which IS the marker retirement that sub-prefix (3) exists to do.
theSecondBlocker.migrationRisk: Not free. A measured obstacle: the host's own opening events carry `undefined` members, and the journal canonicalizer refuses them — `EventJournalCanonicalizationError: JCS cannot represent undefined` out of `canonicalizeCommandIdentityV1`. The mirror swallows this as a shadow mismatch and installs NO head. The new proof suite works around it by JSON round-tripping the opening events; a migration of the two journal suites would hit the same wall on whatever events they commit.

residualConflict.measuredShape: Instrumented at the decision site: `DBG crash-first-batch unavailable true`, `DBG post-command-compatible unavailable true`, `DBG post-command-blocked-digest-mismatch unavailable true`, `DBG post-command-blocked-unsupported-effective-generation unavailable true` - i.e. branch port PRESENT, capability database NOT open, marker PRESENT. Ruling (1) blocks exactly that, so `isJournalAuthorityEnabled()` is false where the suite asserts true (journalAuthorityRollbackProof.test.ts:317). These suites build `new DurableMatchStore({ path: target.file })` with no `capabilityDb` and never initialize SQLiteService.
residualConflict.whyItIsATension: Ruling (2) named the rollback assertions as staying green, and ruling (1) is what stops them. The two are consistent everywhere EXCEPT this shape, where the head's existence is unknowable.
residualConflict.argumentForRelaxing: The marker and the mirrored head AGREE BY CONSTRUCTION today: the marker writes `MATCH_BASELINE_BRANCH_ID` ('main') / `MATCH_BASELINE_FIRST_GENERATION` (1), and the mirror's genesis backfill produces the same branch id and generation (verified in the S3a review's derivability table). The divergence row 4 pins is a synthetic shape no production writer can currently produce. So blocking here refuses a match whose marker head would have been identical to the unreadable one, at the cost of 4 pinned proofs.
residualConflict.argumentForKeeping: It is the literal one-way-boundary rule the parent set, and it stays correct the moment any writer can produce a head that disagrees with the marker - which is precisely what the cutover introduces.
residualConflict.theOneLineChoice: Either (A) keep ruling (1) and migrate those 4 assertions onto capability-backed stores (scope growth, and it drags in the JCS-undefined obstacle recorded under `theSecondBlocker.migrationRisk`), or (B) narrow ruling (1) to honour the marker when the head is unreadable - i.e. `unavailable` behaves as `not-started` - which lands 0 regressions and reduces the proof suite to 6 rows by deleting row 1. NOT decided here; ruling (1) is implemented as written and the tree is left red rather than weakened silently.

resolution.rule: Ruling (1) is NARROWED for the mode-off transition window: `unavailable` behaves as `not-started`, so the marker is honoured where present and legacy answers otherwise. Rationale: the marker and the mirrored head agree by construction today (marker writes MATCH_BASELINE_BRANCH_ID / MATCH_BASELINE_FIRST_GENERATION; the mirror's genesis backfill installs the same branch and generation), so no writer can produce a head that disagrees with the marker it would be substituting for - the refusal is not yet load-bearing.
resolution.deferredTo_1_7: `unavailable + marker present -> blocked/'recovery-fact-read-failed'` BECOMES load-bearing at the cutover (task 1.7), which introduces writers that can move the effective head off the marker's values, and MUST be re-enabled there. Recorded in two places so it cannot be lost: a block comment at the decision site in `ServerMatchHost.selectRecoveredMatchRollbackReader` ('THIS STOPS BEING TRUE AT THE CUTOVER (task 1.7)'), and proof-suite row 1, named 'honours the marker over an unreadable head, which task 1.7 must flip to a refusal', which pins today's behaviour so 1.7 turns it red deliberately rather than silently. The parent carries this into the S7 admission alongside the task 1.3 wording amendment.

Asserts `journal-compatible` carrying branchId 'stale-marker-branch' - i.e. the unreadable head is ignored and the marker wins. Rewriting this row to assert the refusal is the 1.7 task.
